extraction.name: MVBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive Multi-modal Video understanding Benchmark, which covers 20 challenging video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is built by automatically converting public video annotations from 11 existing video datasets into multiple-choice QAs using LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 11 public video benchmarks including STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE and TVQA.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Answer options were randomly sampled from available candidates, shuffled, and processed by an LLM to ensure similar and reasonable lengths.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were filtered based on temporal sensitivity and question difficulty. Short clips with negligible motions and extremely long videos with overly complicated contexts were eliminated, keeping videos primarily ranging from 5s to 35s. Questions requiring more than 10 conditions in CLEVRER were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were automatically generated by converting video annotations into a multiple-choice format via LLMs. ChatGPT was used to generate a question for each video based on task definitions, and answer options were created either directly from ground truth annotations (Template-Based Construction) or generated by ChatGPT (LLM-Based Generation).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset mitigates the bias of answer leakage where longer options tend to be correct by using an LLM to ensure all options have similar lengths. It also avoids biased scoring of LLMs by using a multiple-choice format with ground-truth annotations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the temporal perception capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in the open world.
